title: Throughput of a pipelined block

prereqs.why: The whole question is which of the two numbers — latency or initiation interval — sets throughput.
The reason an II can exceed 1 is a dependency the pipeline cannot resolve in one cycle.

statement:
An HLS tool reports this for a pipelined kernel:

```
Latency (cycles):              12
Initiation interval (cycles):   3
Clock:                     250 MHz
```

The kernel is fed a long, uninterrupted stream of input items.

**How many items per second can it process, in millions of items per second?**

The two numbers mean different things, and only one of them is the answer.
hints: Latency is how long one item takes from entering to leaving. Initiation interval is how many cycles must pass before the *next* item can be started.
If the stream is long, the 12-cycle latency is paid once at the beginning and then never again. What limits the steady state?
250 MHz with a new item accepted every 3 cycles.

payload.hintFormat: Millions of items per second, to one decimal place.
